## Tools

### asusctl and ROG Control Center {#asus-tools}

The daemon, command line and window behind fan curves, profiles and the Slash LED

- **Guide:** [asusctl & ROG Control Center]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/asusctl-rog-control" >}})
- **Only on:** an ASUS laptop
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3306-L3308)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar asusctl rog-control-center
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar asusctl
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar rog-control-center
```

### Hardware monitoring tools {#asus-monitoring}

nvtop, powertop, s-tui, lm_sensors and i2c-tools

- **Guide:** [asusctl & ROG Control Center]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/asusctl-rog-control" >}})
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3309-L3311)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar nvtop powertop s-tui lm_sensors i2c-tools
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar nvtop
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar powertop
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar s-tui
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar lm_sensors
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar i2c-tools
```

## Settings

### Battery charge limit of 80% {#asus-battery-limit}

Stops charging at 80% so the battery lasts longer

- **Guide:** [asusctl & ROG Control Center]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/asusctl-rog-control" >}})
- **Needs:** [asusctl and ROG Control Center](#asus-tools)
- **Only on:** an ASUS laptop
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3312-L3314) · [`on_battery_limit`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1006-L1009) · [`off_battery_limit`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1012-L1013)

Ticking it also ticks what it needs.

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar asusctl rog-control-center

# --- As you ---

# Limit charging to 80%
asusctl battery limit 80
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As you, first ---

# Charge to 100% again
asusctl battery limit 100
```

### Slash LED on AC only {#asus-slash}

The light bar on the lid: off on battery and during sleep

- **Guide:** [asusctl & ROG Control Center]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/asusctl-rog-control" >}})
- **Needs:** [asusctl and ROG Control Center](#asus-tools)
- **Only on:** an ASUS laptop
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3315-L3317) · [`on_slash`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1036-L1039) · [`off_slash`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1042-L1044)

Ticking it also ticks what it needs.

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar asusctl

# --- As you ---

# Slash LED: on AC only
asusctl slash set --enable -b false -s false
```

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As you, first ---

# Slash LED: lit on battery and during sleep again
asusctl slash set --enable -b true -s true
```

### Let asusd own the power profiles {#asus-ppd-mask}

Masks power-profiles-daemon, which fights asusd over the same interface

- **Guide:** [asusctl & ROG Control Center]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/asusctl-rog-control" >}})
- **Only on:** an ASUS laptop
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3318-L3320) · [`on_ppd`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1055-L1059) · [`off_ppd`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1062-L1063) · [`ppd_off_blocker`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1066-L1069)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Mask power-profiles-daemon so asusd owns the power profiles
systemctl mask --now power-profiles-daemon.service
```

- GNOME's own power-mode switch stops working once power-profiles-daemon is masked. Switch profiles with 'asusctl profile next' or ROG Control Center instead.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Unmask power-profiles-daemon
systemctl unmask power-profiles-daemon.service
```

## Fixes

### Brightness in every GPU mode {#backlight-fix}

Without it brightness is dead in Integrated mode (kernel parameter and modprobe rule). Needs a reboot

- **Guide:** [Known Issues]({{< relref "/docs/known-issues" >}})
- **Only on:** the Zephyrus G16 (GA605WV)
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3321-L3324) · [`on_backlight`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1118-L1123) · [`off_backlight`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1126-L1129)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Apply the brightness fix with zephyrus-backlight.py (checked against the SHA-256 built into this setup)
python3 zephyrus-backlight.py enable --silent
# zephyrus-backlight.py is the copy next to quicksetup.py, or else
#   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/main/src/static/scripts/zephyrus-backlight.py
# It only runs when its SHA-256 is 47999987b8dba31fed6f8931a3ef50d23ed0e8dad32dbb890a40c2f5f92c087f
#   which is the one published at https://zephyrus-linux.thectic.nl/scripts/zephyrus-backlight.py
# It asks for your password once and changes, as root:
#   the kernel parameter acpi_backlight=native, wherever this machine keeps its kernel parameters:
#     Limine (CachyOS): two lines appended to /etc/default/limine, then limine-update
#         # Added by zephyrus-backlight.py: the Zephyrus G16 brightness fix
#         KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+="acpi_backlight=native"
#     GRUB: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub (the old file is kept as /etc/default/grub.zephyrus-backlight.bak), then grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
#     ostree (Bazzite): rpm-ostree kargs --append-if-missing=acpi_backlight=native
#     systemd-boot: refused, the guide has the manual steps
#   the modprobe rule /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-wmi-ec-backlight.conf (a different rule that is already there is kept in /var/lib/zephyrus-backlight/)
# If limine-update or grub-mkconfig fails, the old file is put back. Both parts are read at boot.
```

- This machine boots with Limine: limine-update rebuilds the boot images, which takes a minute or more and prints nothing until it is done.
- Needs a reboot: the brightness fix.

**Left for you after ticking it (limine)**

1. zephyrus-backlight.py handles Limine itself (it edits /etc/default/limine and runs limine-update); the guide has the manual steps if you prefer them

**Left for you after ticking it (grub)**

1. zephyrus-backlight.py handles GRUB itself; the guide has the manual steps if you prefer them

**Left for you after ticking it (systemd-boot)**

1. Only if zephyrus-backlight.py refuses systemd-boot:
2. Add acpi_backlight=native to LINUX_OPTIONS in /etc/sdboot-manage.conf, then: sudo sdboot-manage gen
3. Add the modprobe rule from the guide to /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-wmi-ec-backlight.conf
4. Reboot

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Remove the brightness fix with zephyrus-backlight.py (checked against the SHA-256 built into this setup)
python3 zephyrus-backlight.py disable --silent
# zephyrus-backlight.py is the copy next to quicksetup.py, or else
#   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/main/src/static/scripts/zephyrus-backlight.py
# It only runs when its SHA-256 is 47999987b8dba31fed6f8931a3ef50d23ed0e8dad32dbb890a40c2f5f92c087f
#   which is the one published at https://zephyrus-linux.thectic.nl/scripts/zephyrus-backlight.py
# It asks for your password once and changes, as root:
#   takes acpi_backlight=native out of the kernel parameters again:
#     Limine: removes exactly those two lines from /etc/default/limine, then limine-update
#     GRUB: puts back the value GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT had before, from the backup, then grub-mkconfig
#     ostree (Bazzite): rpm-ostree kargs --delete-if-present=acpi_backlight=native
#   removes /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-wmi-ec-backlight.conf, but only while it is still exactly the rule this script wrote (a rule that was there before comes back from /var/lib/zephyrus-backlight/)
```

- Without the fix, brightness does not work in Integrated mode.
- Needs a reboot: removing the brightness fix.
